verses.text: Open your doors, Lebanon, so fire can burn your cedars.
Wail, cypress tree, because the cedar has fallen and the splendid trees are ruined. Wail, oaks of Bashan, because the thick forest has come down.
Listen to the shepherds cry—their glory is gone! Hear the young lions roar—the Jordan’s thicket has been destroyed!
The LORD my God says, “Care for the flock marked for slaughter.
“Their buyers kill them and go unpunished. Those who sell them say, ‘Praise the LORD, I’m rich!’ Even their own shepherds have no pity on them.
“I will no longer spare the people of this land,” says the LORD. “I’ll hand each person over to a neighbor and to the king. They’ll batter the land, and I won’t rescue anyone from them.”
So I cared for the flock marked for slaughter, especially the oppressed ones. I took two staffs: one I called Favor, the other Unity. Then I cared for the flock.
Within one month I got rid of the three shepherds. I had grown tired of them, and they had come to hate me.
Then I said, “I won’t care for you anymore. Let the dying die, and let those doomed to be cut off be cut off. Let the ones who remain eat one another’s flesh.”
I took my staff Favor and broke it, ending the covenant I had made with all the peoples.
That covenant was broken that day. The oppressed sheep watching me knew it was the LORD’s word.
I told them, “If you think it’s right, pay me my wages. If not, keep them.” So they weighed out thirty pieces of silver for me.
The LORD told me, “Throw that magnificent price they valued me at to the potter!” I took the thirty silver pieces and threw them to the potter in the LORD’s house.
Then I broke my other staff, Unity, ending the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
The LORD said to me, “Once again, take the equipment of a foolish shepherd.

“I’m about to raise up a shepherd in the land who won’t care for the ones cut off, search for those scattered, heal the injured, or feed the healthy. Instead, he’ll eat the fat sheep and tear their hooves apart.
“Woe to the worthless shepherd who abandons the flock! May the sword strike his arm and his right eye. May his arm wither completely and his right eye go blind!”
